title: cli: app branding assets are served only from `<cwd>/assets` (or `OS_RUNTIME_ASSETS_DIR`) and silently skipped when that directory is absent — an artifact boot from any other directory draws a broken logo and favicon, with no warning
body: Filing gate: **① product defect with reach measured. Class (a).** reach: every signed-in page of an app whose `branding.logo` / `favicon` point at `/runtime/assets/*`, when the server is started outside the app's project directory. Measured on `@objectstack/*` 17.7.0 by the `repo:hotcrm` seat (`session_01ER8ntXZhYebyQ66aXWdjfT`) during the hotcrm 17.7.0 upgrade (hotcrm PR #2008), on the maintainer's word: 「5. 品牌 logo 容易悄悄丢失 … 以上立卡」. **Who acts on it:** objectstack triage routes it, likely `domain:cli`. ⛔ Not a claim. ## Measured hotcrm's app declares `branding: { logo: '/runtime/assets/icon.svg', favicon: '/runtime/assets/icon.svg' }` (`src/sales/apps/crm.app.ts:61–63`). The file ships in the repo at `assets/icon.svg`. | boot | `GET /runtime/assets/icon.svg` | console | | --- | --- | --- | | `objectstack start --artifact /objectstack.json`, cwd = `` holding only the artifact | **404** | top-left logo is a broken image; no boot line mentions it | | same, after copying `assets/` into `` | 200 `image/svg+xml` | logo drawn | The maintainer noticed it in the screenshots before anyone else did (「左上角 logo是没显示出来吗」). ## Code reading (`origin/main` `8caa131e52`) - `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:3717–3723`: `runtimeAssetsDir = process.env.OS_RUNTIME_ASSETS_DIR?.trim() || path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'assets')`. The comment beside it: *"Silently skips if no assets directory exists."* - `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts:614–615`: `if (!fs.existsSync(assetsDir)) return;`, so the route is not mounted at all. - The compiled artifact carries no asset files, so an artifact copied to a host, container or other directory without the app's `assets/` loses its branding. ## Why it matters - The artifact is the deployable unit, and the docs present `--artifact` and `OS_ARTIFACT_PATH` as the deployment shape. An app's own logo then depends on a directory that travels separately and that nothing checks. - The failure is silent on both sides: no boot warning, and only an `` 404 in the browser console. ## A direction, for triage to rule on (⛔ not a ruling) - At boot, when a loaded app's `branding.logo` / `favicon` names `/runtime/assets/` and that file is not servable, print one warning naming the app, the file, the directory searched and `OS_RUNTIME_ASSETS_DIR`. - Longer term: carry the files an app's branding references in the artifact, or a sidecar the artifact names, so the deployable unit is complete. ## Not measured A cloud or Docker deployment. The reading above is the CLI `start` / `serve` path only. ## Duplicate check Semantic issue search on objectstack, *branding logo runtime assets 404 artifact deployment assets directory not packaged*: 0 hits. Positive control: `createRuntimeAssetsPlugin` resolves in the code reading above. Dedupe words: runtime assets 404 · branding logo broken · OS_RUNTIME_ASSETS_DIR · assets not in artifact · silently skips assets --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_
